```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```
1. Introduction
This analysis explores factors that influence graduate school admission. The response variable admit is binary (1 = admitted, 0 = not admitted). Predictors include GRE score, GPA, and undergraduate institution rank (1 = highest rank).

2. Load Data and Packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

admissions <- read.csv("../../Data/GradSchool_Admissions.csv")

head(admissions)
summary(admissions)
```

3. Data Exploration
```{r}
mean(admissions$admit)
ggplot(admissions, aes(gre)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)
ggplot(admissions, aes(gre)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)
ggplot(admissions, aes(factor(rank))) +
  geom_bar()
```

4. Data Preparation
```{r}
admissions$rank <- factor(admissions$rank)
```

5. Logistic Regression Model
```{r}
model <- glm(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank,
             data = admissions,
             family = binomial)

summary(model)
```

6. Predicted Probabilities
```{r}
admissions$prob <- predict(model, type = "response")
head(admissions)
```

7. Simple Interpretation
-Higher GRE scores increase admission probability
-Higher GPA increases admission probability
-Lower-ranked schools (higher rank number) reduce admission probability compared to rank 1

8. Conclusion
GRE, GPA, and undergraduate institution rank are important predictors of graduate school admission.
